claims.why_uncovered: The screen asks whether the filer depreciates the property under ADS. That is a question about what the filer does, not what the law requires. The screen also names some ADS triggers on its own: use mainly outside the United States, tax-exempt use property, and tax-exempt bond financed property. It leaves out four other required-ADS cases: imported property under an executive order, the section 263A(d)(3) election (which forces ADS on all property the farmer places in service that year, not just farm classes), qualified improvement property held by an electing real property trade or business (QIP is otherwise in scope), and 10-year-or-longer property held by an electing farming business. A filer in one of these cases who has been using GDS would answer no and get GDS rates plus a special allowance, but property required to use ADS gets no special allowance.
